decisions.reason: The question covers train–test color shifts and retaining color cues, but omits generalization to underrepresented colors. The result addresses rare classes separately.
The method mentions sharing shape features across hues and using discrete rotations. It omits input-layer filter weight sharing and the feature-map hue dimension that shifts with the input hue.

The poster identifies both tasks and describes the long-tailed class labels. It omits the balanced test set and does not explain how hue dispersion changes the informativeness of color about digit identity.

The long-tailed panel legend identifies vanilla Z2CNN, grayscale Z2CNN, and coset-pooled CECNN. Approximate parameter matching, the absence of augmentation, and averaging over ten random initializations are missing.
The eight natural-image benchmarks and their ResNet backbone assignments are absent.
The natural-image comparisons, including the full and hybrid CE-ResNet variants, parameter matching, rotation count, color-jitter conditions, CIConv-W, and AugMix, are absent.
The poster does not distinguish original-test accuracy from mean accuracy over hue shifts from −180° to +180°. Panel (b) plots accuracy against dataset standard deviation.
The natural-image accuracy and robustness findings, the complementary role of color jitter, and qualifications by dataset and model variant are absent.
The poster omits compute cost, potential capacity loss from narrowing networks, and approximate equivariance caused by clipping or reprojection after RGB rotation.

notes: The caption correctly maps panel (a) to the long-tailed task and panel (b) to the color-biased task. The figure’s legends and ticks are small, particularly the class labels in panel (a). The rotation symbol after 120 renders as a solid square, and the caption’s distribution formula has detached indices. The question heading cites p. 1, while the checklist cites p. 2 for its supporting quote. The supplied excerpts cannot establish whether p. 1 also supports the question or independently verify the exact reported accuracies. Counts reflect observed errors in the supplied evidence.
